entries.title: I Kings 2:3
segments: To walk in the way of the Lord by keeping his commandments is, in rulers as well as people, not only right and honorable, but the surest means of permanent prosperity; while the contrary course, in rulers or people, is dishonorable and ruinous.

entries.title: I Kings 2:4
segments: Continue; more literally, establish; that is, continue to fulfil his promise, which was made conditional upon the obedience of David's successors on the throne.

entries.title: I Kings 2:7
segments: The compassion of parents, and their readiness to do good, especially to the distressed, are often owned of God in blessings on their children, by leading them to imitate the good examples of their parents, and thus to become partakers of their reward.

entries.title: I Kings 2:9
segments: With blood; put him to a violent death for his crimes.  David judged it proper, at the time when Shimei met him, to give him his oath that he would not put him to death; but he felt that for the good of his kindgom such conduct ought to be punished with death, and Solomon was free to treat him according to his deserts.

entries.title: I Kings 2:15
segments: The kingdom was mine; his meaning was, that it belonged to him as David's oldest living son.  His second son Chileab,

, seems to have been already dead. 
 
God in his providence raises up one and puts down another; and when he has determined to elevate an individual to great power and influence, no efforts of men, however wisely directed or diligently pursued, will prevent it.

entries.title: I Kings 2:19
segments: No elevation of wise children will prevent them from loving and honoring aged parents, and as far as may be consistent with duty, complying with their requests.

entries.title: I Kings 2:22
segments:
Ask for him the kingdom; by this Solomon intimated to his mother, that, considering the relation Abishag had sustained to David, Adonijah's request for her implied an assertion of his right to the kingdom; for this was, according to the custom of those days, the way in which an usurper proceeded in respect to the concubines of his predecessor. 
 
No filal respect or affection, and no promises or engagements, should ever lead men to do what is morally wrong.

entries.title: I Kings 2:23
segments: God do so to me; put me to death, if I do not put Adonijah to death.

entries.title: I Kings 2:24
segments: Made me a house; secured him a posterity to inherit the throne after him.

entries.title: I Kings 2:26
segments:
Anathoth; a city in Benjamin. 
 
No elevation or official sanctity should be permitted to cover the guilt of crime, nor should the openly criminal or vicious be continued in any public employment.

entries.title: I Kings 2:27
segments: Abiathar, who was of the house of Eli, in the line of Ithamar, had been the high-priest after the death of Ahimelech his father.  Zadok, who succeeded him as high-priest, was descended from Aaron by the line of Eleazar.

entries.title: I Kings 2:28
segments: Fled unto the tabernacle--the altar; as a place of safety.  See note to

entries.title: I Kings 2:31
segments: Do as he hath said; slay him at the altar.  Solomon put substantial justice above the observance of an ancient usage.

entries.title: I Kings 2:33
segments: Shall there be peace; by putting Joab to death, they would be free from the guilt of conniving at the murders he had committed.

entries.title: I Kings 2:39
segments: By a too eager desire that others should serve them, men may occasion their own ruin.
